about: The everyday Japanese form of a club's name, where the Japanese label Wikidata holds for it is a long transliteration of an abbreviation or of a formal name that Japanese media do not use (BC Lions: ブリティッシュ・コロンビア・ライオンズ for BCライオンズ; Liverpool F.C.: リヴァプールFC for リバプール), a Wikipedia page title with a disambiguator or 'history of' added, or the name of the club in another period. Keyed by the club's Wikidata item. `ja` is what the atlas shows as `clubJa`; Wikidata's own label is kept as `aliasesJa` so that a search by it still finds the club. `kind` says why: abbreviation, formal (a formal name or a suffix such as FC), title (a page title and not a name) or era (the label is the club's name in another period). `note` is the source: what was checked, where and when. Added by hand and checked by a Japanese-language reviewer (2026-10-13); `aliases` are further names the club is found by, kept beside Wikidata's label. The build leaves every other club's label as Wikidata has it.

Q919062.note: BC is the everyday abbreviation of British Columbia, as written in Japanese sources. ja.wikipedia.org has a page titled BCライオンズ (checked 2026-10-13).

Q631.note: Japanese media say インテル or インテル・ミラノ; インテルナツィオナーレ・ミラノ is the full formal name. ja.wikipedia.org redirects インテル・ミラノ to インテルナツィオナーレ・ミラノ (checked 2026-10-13). Media often say インテル alone (kept as an alias); インテル・ミラノ is also common and tells it from Inter Miami.

Q15799.note: CA is the initials of Club Atlético and is not said as a part of the name. ja.wikipedia.org redirects リーベル・プレート to CAリーベル・プレート (checked 2026-10-13).
